subject: Smoothing runway + proposed GPU top-up for Q3 usage surge
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@cloudwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T15:12:00Z
Subject: Smoothing runway + proposed GPU top-up for Q3 usage surge

Alex —

Quick note after reviewing last week's usage report: your Q3 inference volumes are picking up faster than forecasted. The capacity snapshot (attached) shows sustained 68–74% GPU utilization across peak windows and a filling burst queue that has pushed tail latency above your SLOs on several days.

High-level recommendation: a modest reserved top-up now to smooth the runway, plus a short-term burst capacity buffer during the upcoming marketing surge. Specifically: add 18 reserved A100-class slots (3 staggered tranches of 6 over the next 6 weeks) and a 12-GPU burst pool for two months. This reduces fill-rate churn and keeps tail latency within 99th percentile targets while giving you runway to evaluate longer-term commit sizing.

I attached a capacity snapshot and a quick heatmap. If you want, we can turn this into a formal amendment and pricing addendum for procurement. Ben — can you help with a draft SOW amendment and an initial pricing sketch?

Next steps I propose:
- Internal review + pricing sketch (Ben) — 48 hours
- Walkthrough with CloudWave engineering — call Wed 5/12
- Draft amendment sent to procurement by Fri 5/14

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- capacity-snapshot-may2027.csv (CSV with per-cluster utilization + 7d projection)
- usage-heatmap-may2027.png (visual of hourly GPU load)
From: Alex Chen <alex@cloudwave.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudwave.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Smoothing runway + proposed GPU top-up for Q3 usage surge

Neha —

Appreciate the fast follow. The snapshot aligns with what we've observed: nightly model retrains and a new search ranking test increased steady-state token generation by ~22% over two weeks. A few clarifications before the call:

1) Can you confirm whether the 18 reserved slots are assumed at the same instance spec we run today (A100 40GB), or are you proposing a mix (some A10s for lower-memory workloads)?
2) What's the expected monthly delta in cost (ballpark) for the reserved tranches vs. using burst alone?
3) For the 12-GPU burst pool, can that be time-windowed (peak hours only) to reduce spend?

Procurement: we'll need a redlineable amendment and an estimate we can run through finance.

Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | CloudWave Labs
alex@cloudwave.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T14:25:00Z
Subject: RE: Smoothing runway + proposed GPU top-up for Q3 usage surge — internal pricing sketch

Neha / Karthik —

Attached a quick pricing sketch and an initial amendment outline (I exported a compact CSV with utilization windows). Key assumptions I used:
- Reserved tranches: 18 x A100(40GB) at a 12-month blended rate of $X,XXX/GPU/mo (discounted for an immediate commit).
- Burst pool: 12 GPUs billed at usage hours with an applied capped burst rate during defined peak windows (we can implement schedule-based routing to constrain to 6am–10am & 6pm–10pm PT).
- Estimated monthly delta: reserved + burst nets ~ +27% on current monthly spend but reduces on-demand tail spend by ~43% and improves 99th latency by ~350ms on peak days.

Operational ask for Karthik: can we prepare a gating policy that auto-fallbacks to burst (capped) if reserved utilization exceeds 88% for more than 3 consecutive 10-minute windows? That should protect stability without manual intervention.

I'll turn the sketch into a redline-ready amendment draft once Neha confirms we want blended A100s vs mix.

—Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments:
- redwood-amendment-draft-v1.pdf
- pricing-sketch-may11.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T16:37:00Z
Subject: RE: Smoothing runway + proposed GPU top-up for Q3 usage surge — gating policy + operational notes

Ben / team —

I can build the gating policy for automated fallback. Notes from a runtime/ops perspective:

- Gating thresholds: trigger when reserved pool > 88% for 3 consecutive samples of 10 minutes (as suggested). When triggered, route new requests into burst pool until reserved utilization dips below 70% for a sustained 30-minute window.
- Time-windowed burst: yes — we can schedule the burst pool to be live only during configured peak windows. That will be enforced on the routing layer and transparent to CloudWave.
- Mixed instance spec: suggest splitting 18 reserved as 12 x A100(40GB) + 6 x A10(24GB) so memory-heavy training/inference stays on A100s while lower-memory tasks use A10s. This reduces blended cost by ~12% while keeping latency SLAs intact.
- Telemetry: enable token-level latency traces and a quick dashboard widget (we'll share a short-lived link) so CloudWave can watch 99th percentile improvements post-commit.

I can prototype the policy and the dashboard today and have it ready for the Wed 5/12 call.

Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Alex Chen <alex@cloudwave.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudwave.ai>
Date: 2027-05-13T20:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Smoothing runway + proposed GPU top-up for Q3 usage surge

Neha/Ben/Karthik —

Thanks — this looks good and aligns with what finance wants to see. Procurement, pls expect an amendment from Redwood next week for review. A couple of items on our side:

- Confirm we can time-window the burst pool (yes per Karthik) — great.
- We prefer the mixed spec approach (12 A100 + 6 A10) to reduce cost while protecting heavy workloads.
- Can you add a 30-day exit clause on the two-month burst extension in case upstream traffic normalizes earlier? Procurement will need that for approval.

If you can get the redlineable amendment and the estimated monthly delta into DocuSign by 5/17, procurement will run it through finance the same day. We'll be prepared to route signatures the week of 5/17.

Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | CloudWave Labs
